i Zulu Date: a plain calendar date — use this for everyday flights where dispatch just gives you a normal date. Julian Date: enter Julian Day + Zulu time instead — use this when your release, load plan, or log already gives you a day-of-year number, so you're not converting it yourself. tap to switch date format (applies to Departure & Arrival) i Turn this on if your trip crosses a year boundary — for example, departing in late December and arriving in January. Otherwise the day-of-year number alone is all you need.

Trip summary i Off by default so the app never uses the network on its own. Turn this on, then tap "Get arrival weather" whenever you actually want a live check — it only reaches the internet at that moment, never automatically. Needs a specific airport for Destination, not just a city.

Flight duration i This is the raw time between departure and arrival Zulu times — it does not account for wind, thunderstorm avoidance, routing delays, etc.
—
Arriving locally
—
Enter departure and arrival details to see local times and any date-line crossing.

Variables i Every duration here is yours to set — nothing is pre-loaded from any regulation. Most are measured before or after takeoff (from the Flight tab), but a few chain off each other instead — Crew Rest is before Show, Last Ambien is before Alert, and so on. The label under each field shows exactly what it's measured from. Duration format is H+MM, e.g. 4+15 for 4 hours 15 minutes.

Set each duration and what it's measured from — shown under each field. The Timing tab does the rest.

Timing

Computed straight from your Variables. Each row still toggles Local/Zulu for display.

Crew Text

Pulls the timeline above plus the Flight tab into one short, copyable summary.

Tap "Generate crew timing" to build the summary.
Runs entirely on your device. No accounts, no tracking, no network requests — works offline once loaded, unless you turn on Arrival Weather. City and airport lookups use your browser's built-in time zone data.
